scratch.title: Everyday Sunnah
scratch.sourceNote: Brief paraphrases of hadith meanings; follow the links to read the sources.

sunnahs.quote: Do not belittle any good deed, even meeting your brother with a cheerful face.
Allah loves gentleness in every matter.
Whoever does not show mercy will not be shown mercy.
The best among you are those with the best character.
Pause before an ordinary task and consider the good you intend. The hadith connects deeds with intentions.
Choose a manageable good deed and return to it regularly. The hadith values consistency even in small deeds.
Mention Allah’s name, eat with your right hand, and take what is nearest to you in a shared dish.
Let your words bring good. When there is nothing good to say, silence can help prevent harmful speech.
The hadith connects faith with avoiding harm to neighbours and treating guests generously.
Make ablution before bed and lie on your right side. Both actions appear in the Prophet’s guidance.
Do not postpone charity just because you can give only a little. The hadith mentions even half a date.
Share the greeting of peace. The hadith describes salam as a way to strengthen love among believers.
Helping someone through difficulty is a meaningful good deed. The hadith encourages support and easing hardship.
Seeking beneficial knowledge is worth the effort. Read thoughtfully, check sources, and ask a knowledgeable person about what is unclear.
Gentleness makes actions better. Try expressing the same idea calmly, without harshness or humiliation.
Alhamdulillah expresses praise of Allah. The hadith describes the significance of these words, remembrance, prayer and patience.

knowledge.title: Knowledge & benefit
knowledge.intro: Short, grounded reminders for a thoughtful day.

cards.label: Generosity
cards.title: Charity does not diminish
cards.text: The Prophet ﷺ taught that charity does not diminish wealth. Even a small, regular act of support can nourish gratitude and care for people.

cards.label: Remembrance
cards.title: Begin the morning with dhikr
cards.text: The Qur’an calls believers to remember Allah often. A few quiet minutes of mindful dhikr can be a gentle anchor for the day.

cards.label: Night
cards.title: A quiet Tahajjud moment
cards.text: The voluntary night prayer is a chance to turn to Allah in private. Start small and do not turn voluntary worship into an unbearable burden.

items.q: How do I use the counter?
items.a: Tap the circle once for each dhikr. Free mode has no target. The reset button clears the current count.
Choose After prayer. The app moves through Subhanallah, Alhamdulillah and Allahu akbar 33 times each, then the full final tahlil once. Source: Sahih Muslim 597a.
The round stops when complete. Choose Another round to start again.

items.q: How do I show only the circle?
items.a: Tap the focus icon near the title. Exit with ×, Escape, or a two-finger touch.
Automatically in this browser, when local storage is available. Clearing browser data removes it. Counts do not sync across devices.
After a complete first visit over HTTPS, the main app is cached. Quran audio and source links need internet access.

items.q: Can I put Nur on my home screen?
items.a: Use your browser menu. In Safari on iPhone choose Share, then Add to Home Screen.

items.q: Why is there no sound or vibration?
items.a: Check Nur settings and device volume. Sound starts after interaction. Vibration depends on browser and device support.
Scratch part of the cover or tap Reveal card. Next shows another reminder.
The cards contain brief paraphrases and practical reminders, with source links. Consult a qualified scholar for religious rulings.

items.q: How do I clear all data?
items.a: Open settings, choose Clear local app data and confirm. Only this browser’s Nur data is cleared.
Swipe horizontally on empty reading space. Controls and the scratch card keep their own gestures.
